title: Transparent degradation and priming safeguards for hosted GPU pools
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Summary: After the Feb GPU exhaustion incident we observed rapid queue buildup due to simultaneous tenant bursts and tight autoscaler hysteresis. This ticket defines a set of low-risk engineering changes, operational runbooks, and telemetry additions to provide transparent degradation (graceful deferral), proactive priming, and improved admission control for hosted GPU pools. Goals are to (1) reduce tail latency and massive queue amplification during pool stress, (2) keep critical customer traffic live via graceful degradation policies, and (3) improve detectability and automated priming to reduce MTTR for capacity events. This work should be deployable behind a kill-switch and validated by a chaos/traffic-sim testbed.
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after incident postmortem. Initial scope workshop with SRE, runtime, and product scheduled.
2025-02-13: SRE proposed incremental admission backoffs (per-tenant token-bucket decay + jitter) and a fast-path for small inference requests. Action: prototype admission algorithm in sandbox.

2025-02-14: Runtime team flagged risk: immediate backoff may increase cold-starts that trigger autoscaler. Decision: pair admission smoothing with a lightweight priming flow to prewarm slots for tiers with steady historical traffic.

2025-02-15: Design review: Console UX will surface transparent degradation status per-tenant with estimated retry-after hints. Product requested an optional customer opt-in for aggressive deferral to preserve SLAs for paying tiers.

2025-02-17: Prototype admission controller merged to feature branch. Initial synthetic tests show 30% reduction in queue amplification with <5% increase in autoscale events. Need longer-run load tests.
2025-02-18: Added telemetry: new Grafana panel for 'admission-backoff-rate', 'prewarm-fill-rate', and 'degradation-events-by-tenant'. Draft runbook for responding to repeated degradation created.
2025-02-20: Begin integration tests with tenant-simulator. Next: canary rollout to 5% of pools and a production fast rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout shows reduced queue length growth in >=90th percentile buckets under synthetic 2x burst traffic compared to baseline
Console displays per-tenant degradation status and suggested retry-after header for client SDKs
Runbook steps for SRE and on-call include automated priming trigger and safe rollback instructions
Telemetry emitted for every semantically meaningful event: admission decision, prewarm attempt, prewarm success/failure
Feature behind runtime feature-flag and can be disabled without infra changes

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive early shedding reduces queue growth but can harm client-perceived availability; solution is to combine shedding with informative retry semantics and an optional premium tenant escape hatch.
We must avoid hard-coded tenant thresholds. Plan to base priming on moving-window percentiles per tenant and global pool occupancy signals.

Security: priming requests will be scoped and authenticated using existing internal service credentials; security review required for telemetry exposure to Console (sensitive tenant IDs should be redacted).
Operationally, aim for a 2-minute detection-to-priming window for common bursts; keep priming lease short (30-120s) to limit resource waste.
